items.title: JJ Johnson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: His name was Fred Beckett. He was a brilliant trombonist... I had never heard a trombone play that kind of linear conceptualizing... It was remarkable, and it left an indelible mark on me

ctx.x: When did you first feel like this might be what you wanted to do as your life’s work?

It was during the cycle of activity that involved Vincent Stewart, Erroll Grandy, Eldridge Morrison, Merrill Laswell, and these people that we are recalling. We were all Lester Young addicts. We were Lester Young-oholics. We knew all of his solos on every record, note by note. All of us, any of us could sing any of Lester Young’s solos. By now I was really hooked on Lester Young and people like Lester Young – the other prominent, outstanding soloists of that era – and it was then that I knew that somehow I would…
